Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis  
Details: The issue report states that using ExtendedMessageFormat with a custom format registry and a pattern containing single quotes causes an OutOfMemoryError. The failing test is constructing an ExtendedMessageFormat with a pattern containing single quotes:  
```java
String pattern = "it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!";
ExtendedMessageFormat emf = new ExtendedMessageFormat(pattern, registry);
```

The constructor ExtendedMessageFormat(String, Map) calls another constructor ExtendedMessageFormat(String, Locale, Map), which sets the registry and then calls applyPattern(pattern). In applyPattern, when a registry is present (non-null), it parses the pattern manually.

The parsing loop in applyPattern treats single quotes (QUOTE) by calling appendQuotedString. The code in appendQuotedString handles escaped quotes (two single quotes) by appending one quote and advancing the parse position. It uses a loop to consume characters inside quotes until it finds a closing quote.

The bug likely happens because appendQuotedString does not correctly handle nested or consecutive quotes when a custom registry is used, causing the parsing position not to advance properly or causing infinite recursion/loop. This would cause applyPattern to loop indefinitely or consume excessive memory, leading to OutOfMemoryError.

Specifically, the test pattern has multiple single quotes and a sub-format "{0,lower}". The interaction between quote parsing and format parsing with the custom registry may cause wrong position advancement. The code at line 421:  
```java
if (escapingOn && c[start] == QUOTE) {
    return appendTo == null ? null : appendTo.append(QUOTE);
}
```
looks suspicious because it returns early but does not advance position, which in combination with other calls might cause repeated parsing of the same character.

Similarly, the while loop in applyPattern uses pos.getIndex() to iterate but if pos is not advanced properly inside appendQuotedString or other methods, it will be stuck.

Hence, the root cause is a bug in ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern combined with appendQuotedString when handling patterns with single quotes and a custom registry, causing infinite looping or repeated processing that triggers OutOfMemoryError.

I can inspect more methods involved in pattern parsing/format retrieval if needed next.
org.apache.commons.lang.text.ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.lang.text.ExtendedMessageFormat.appendQuotedString(java.lang.String,java.text.ParsePosition,java.lang.StringBuffer,boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
